issues: The quote is verbatim (--check FOUND), but it does not support the label 'Countries whose privacy authorities drafted the Madrid Resolution'. The 'fifty countries' sentence comes from the promotional preface signed by Artemi Rallo Lombarte, Director of the Spanish Data Protection Agency, and no list of the fifty is given.

The same PDF records who actually drafted the text. The AEPD invited every accredited authority to join a preparatory Working Group. The group met in January and June 2009 and drafted the Joint Proposal. Its footnoted membership list, 'AUTHORITIES BELONGING TO THE WORKING GROUP', names 23 authorities from 17 countries or territories, plus the European Data Protection Supervisor. The 17 are Austria, Belgium, Burkina Faso, Canada (2), Czech Republic, France, Germany (3), Hong Kong, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, New Zealand, Portugal, Slovenia, Spain (4), Switzerland and the UK. So the formal drafters came from 17 jurisdictions, not 50. The 50 is the Spanish DPA's own broader count of the countries whose 'privacy guarantors' contributed.
The source institution should name the author of the quoted preface: the AEPD Director, writing for the Conference.

fieldFixes.label: Countries whose privacy authorities contributed to the Madrid Resolution (Spanish DPA's own count)
fieldFixes.notes: The figure of fifty comes from the Spanish DPA director's preface ('privacy guarantors from fifty countries'); the fifty are not listed. The formal drafting Working Group was smaller: 23 authorities from 17 countries or territories, plus the European Data Protection Supervisor. It met in January and June 2009. The International Conference welcomed the text in Madrid on 5 November 2009.

sourceFixes.institution: Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD), for the International Conference of Data Protection and Privacy Commissioners (PDF hosted by the Global Privacy Assembly)

issues: The quote 'Of the 20 conferences before 1999, only five were held outside Europe.' is verbatim on the GPA history page (--check FOUND). The same page's own list of conferences contradicts it. The 1st to 20th conferences (1979–1998) were held in Bonn, Ottawa, Paris, London, Stockholm, Vienna, Luxembourg, Lisbon, Quebec, Oslo, Berlin, Paris, Strasbourg, Sydney, Manchester, The Hague, Copenhagen, Ottawa, Brussels and Santiago de Compostela. Only four of these are outside Europe: Ottawa 1980, Quebec 1987, Sydney 1992 and Ottawa 1996.

The page's own narrative agrees with four: 'primarily in European locations with an occasional foray to Canada and one trip down-under to Sydney, Australia, in 1992'. That is three Canadian meetings and one Australian. The GPA document archive independently lists the 9th (Quebec 1987), 14th (Sydney 1992) and 18th (Ottawa 1996) conferences. The 'five' probably counts the 21st conference (Hong Kong, 1999), which is not 'before 1999'. The value should be 4.

fieldFixes.notes: Counted from the GPA's own list of conferences: Ottawa 1980, Quebec 1987, Sydney 1992 and Ottawa 1996. The GPA's history text says 'only five', but its list shows four; five is reached only by adding the 21st conference (Hong Kong, 1999).

sourceFixes.quote: The Assembly met for the first 20 years primarily in European locations with an occasional foray to Canada and one trip down-under to Sydney, Australia, in 1992.
sourceFixes.note: Re-fetched the page. The original 'only five' sentence is verbatim but contradicted by the page's own list. The replacement quote is verbatim (--check FOUND). All other conferences from 1 to 20 were in European cities.

issues: All points and quotes check out. All five quotes, including the inline point sources, are verbatim on the free PL&B abstract pages (--check FOUND): 76 (1st ed. 2011), 109 (Jan 2015), 120 (Jan 2017), 132 (Jan 2019), 145 (Jan 2021), 157 (mid-March 2022), 162 (Feb 2023) and 172 (March 2025). The int195 abstract confirms the 2025 note 'as at 15 March 2025'. Greenleaf's own homepage confirms the 2023 note '8th edition': 'Global Tables of Data Privacy Laws and Bills (8th Ed, 2023) 162 countries'. The PL&B April 2025 abstract also refers to the 'Eighth Edition, 2023'. Source dates (2021-02, 2022-04, 2023-02, 2025-06) match the issues: February 2021, April 2022, February 2023 and June 2025.

The note's example of a recount is wrong. It says 'the 2020 decade recount gives 142 by end-2019 vs 132 in the January 2019 edition' to show that recounts are higher 'for the same years'. The two figures describe different cut-offs, January 2019 and end-2019. The PL&B February 2020 abstract says the 10-law gap consists of laws 'enacted or located' since January 2019, so much of it is new 2019 enactments, not recounting. A true same-period example comes from the same abstract: its per-decade counts (10 + 10 + 20 + 40) give 80 countries by end-2009, more than the 76 the 1st edition found in 2011.
The claim that counts include some self-governing territories is supported. The February 2020 abstract refers to 'over 200 countries (including self-governing territories)'. Source added.

fieldFixes.notes: Contemporaneous counts from each edition of Graham Greenleaf's Global Tables and his PL&B assessments. Later recounts can be higher for the same period because laws are 'located' after the fact. Greenleaf's February 2020 decade recount (10 new countries in the 1970s, 10 in the 1980s, 20 in the 1990s and 40 in the 2000s) implies 80 countries by end-2009, more than the 76 the 1st edition identified in 2011. The same recount gives 142 by end-2019, against 132 in the January 2019 edition; those ten were laws enacted or located during 2019. Counts include some self-governing territories.
